title: Segmented prefix stability and grace-window for embedding dedupe & caching
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Goal: Improve cache hit rate and reduce wasted embedding compute by introducing a deterministic segmented-prefix keying strategy plus a configurable grace-window staleness policy for embeddings used by reranking and vector search. This ticket defines the design, acceptance criteria, rollout plan, and instrumentation for a tenant-aware segmented prefix index (deterministic segmenter) with content-hash canonicalization, salted per-tenant hashing to avoid collisions, probabilistic tombstones, and a safety grace window to allow stale hits with degradation controls.
background: We see two recurring problems: 1) high duplication of embedding compute when clients send long near-duplicate prefixes with minor edits, and 2) hard invalidation policies that prematurely evict embeddings causing recompute spikes. Existing patchwork solutions (shingling, naive prefix truncation) either miss edge cases or create cache churn. This design aims to reduce tail latency and unit cost while keeping semantic correctness for reranking/semantic search.
implementation_notes: Deterministic segmenter: tokenize input, compute rolling simhash-like shingles, then map to fixed segments (N=4) by stable boundary heuristics (prefer punctuation + whitespace boundaries).
Content canonicalization: normalize whitespace, punctuation, unicode NFKC, lowercasing for non-language-specific pipelines, then apply tenant salt before hashing.
Key format: tenant_id|model_id|segment_index|seg_hash_v2 to keep keys flat and short.
Grace window: per-tenant configurable time window (default 2h) where stale cache hits are allowed but tagged with staleness metadata and a degrade threshold (max_staleness_similarity_delta).
Tombstone & negative cache: when documents are deleted or embeddings rotated, write a short-lived tombstone entry (TTL=5m) to prevent thundering herd; negative cache writes on transient failures.
Invalidation pipeline: stream invalidation events over Kafka topic 'embed-inval-v2' with idempotent consumer and per-tenant sequence numbers; background compaction job to clear segments.
Fallback behavior: on cache miss, compute embedding; if similar live segment exists (cosine > 0.985) use cached value and mark as reused to avoid recompute.
Backwards compat: provide config toggle (runtime flag) to enable new segmented keys; keep legacy LRU for rollback.
Storage: use existing memcached cluster for hot segments, tier to Redis for warm, and object-store for cold traces; ensure keys < 250 bytes.
Quota & cost: track hit-savings to attribute unit-cost improvements to tenant usage for billing adjustments.
acceptance_criteria: Segmenter generates deterministic segments for same logical text across clients (unit tests + fuzzing).
Cache hit rate for reranking traffic improves by >= 12% on average for test cohort A (internal eval) within 2 weeks of rollout.
95th percentile embedding latency for rerank requests decreases by >= 8ms or recompute cost decreases by >= 10% for medium-load tenants.
Grace-window stale serve path is implemented and logged; stale_served_ratio is < 5% by default and adjustable.
Invalidation events are published and consumers can clear corresponding segments within SLA (target 30s for critical deletes).
Feature gated behind runtime flag with safe rollback in under 15 minutes.
End-to-end integration tests and chaos test to simulate tombstone storms without data loss.
tasks: Proto: implement segmenter library and unit tests (ENG).
Storage: add key schema and Redis tiering changes (Infra).
Invalidation: produce/consume events on Kafka and add compaction job (ENG/Infra).
Runtime: wire graceful stale serve path and telemetry (Runtime team).
API: expose tenant-level config for grace window and similarity thresholds in Console (PM + Console).
E2E tests: create synthetic workload and evaluate hit-rate improvements (SRE + ENG).
Rollout: stage flag -> canary -> 50% -> 100% with automated rollback on error budgets (SRE + ENG).
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: salted tenant hashing could still collide for very similar corpora across tenants. Mitigation: include model_id and short nonce in key and keep per-tenant salt isolated.
Risk: grace-window stale serves could return semantically outdated reranks. Mitigation: set conservative default thresholds and surface staleness in response metadata for clients to opt-out.
Risk: tombstone storms may increase write amplification. Mitigation: batch invalidations and use compacted invalidation log with deduplication.
Risk: added complexity in key schema may increase storage footprint. Mitigation: enforce tight key length limits and reuse compressed hash (base62).
rollout_plan: Week 1: library landed behind flag, unit tests, and basic integration in dev environment.
Week 2: canary rollout for 5 internal tenants; monitor hit rate and latency for 72h.
Week 3: expand to 25% of traffic, run chaos invalidation test, validate tombstone behavior.
Week 4: full rollout if metrics stable; otherwise iterate on thresholds and compaction policy.
Rollback: disable runtime flag -> drain new keys -> compact tombstone log; SRE playbook prepared.
